Posted September 17, 2005
Analysis by Richard Cowan
From April, 2001, see
 We Are Winning! Canadian Medical Marijuana Program: Politically Very Important, Medically and Scientifically Absurd.

After years of delay, Health Canada is finally moving to distribute medical cannabis in drugstores. It will be tested in a pilot project early next year. How time flies when you are not in pain  and not in prison!
See
 How Time Flies  When You Are Not In Pain. Two Articles Document the Governments War on the Sick and Dying.

Over two years ago, in early 2003, Health Canada officials visited The Netherlands to study the Dutch program for selling medical grade cannabis in pharmacies, which finally began in September of 2003.
See
 MarijuanaNews Reported It A Month Ago, But Now Its Official: Dutch Pharmacies Provide Medical cannabis Covered by Health Insurance.

Apparently they learned something in the meantime, because HCs cannabis will supposedly sell for less than half what the Dutch tried to charge. Because most Dutch health insurance would not cover the cost of the cannabis, the government is selling less than a third of what it expected and is losing money. Most patients found it cheaper to continue buying it in coffee shops, some of which give discounts to patients. Consequently, the Dutch may even abandon the project entirely. Also, the current health minister, Hans Hoogervorst, is a prohibitionist who still claims that the medical value of cannabis has never been scientifically proven. That is still the party line at Health Canada.
For more about the Dutch medical cannabis program see
 http://www.cannabisbureau.nl/eng/index.html

HC is looking for a few urban and rural pharmacies for the pilot project. Supposedly, some of the first pharmacies will be in British Columbia, but the need is probably greater in other provinces where medical cannabis is harder to get. On the other hand, there are probably more open-minded pharmacists and doctors in BC, so it will be easier to test.

Originally, HC was going to have the program going last year, but it took a long time to hold consultations with everyone who was not in actual pain.
See
 Health Canadas Office of Cannabis Medical Access' Stakeholder Advisory Committee Includes Physicians for A Smoke Free Canada - Not The Compassion Societies. But It Will Let Them Talk For An Hour

An HC spokesperson said, Ideally, we'd like to run it in more than one province. Once we recruit the pharmacists, we'll make sure (they) receive specialized training in dispensing the marijuana for medical purposes. I would love to be the proverbial fly on the wall at those specialized training sessions. 

Robin O'Brien, a Vancouver pharmacist, was asked by Health Canada to participate as a consultant. CP quotes her as saying that pharmacists can fill a real medical need, but her comments are not very reassuring. 

The CP article has her warning, Some lay people may offer advice at so-called compassion clubs, but rarely is a medically trained professional available to advise on methods of ingestion or to warn about drug interactions.

Pharmacists will need specialized training in how medical marijuana can be administered safely and effectively. Smoking has adverse effects and is discouraged, so that professionals may need to prepare tinctures, where the THC is extracted with alcohol and administered as drops...

Most physicians don't have a lot of interest or expertise in using marijuana for medical purposes, so patients have been getting their information most likely from black-market dealers (or) recreational users.
See
 The British Columbia Medical Association To Vote On Reefer Madness Resolution; MarijuanaNews Offers an Alternative.

In other words, the patients have had to get information from people with actual experience. Oh, the horror!
See
 Eagle Bill, The Loss of A Good Man and Vaporizer Pioneer. Bills Life Will Long Be Recognized As A Rebuke to Medical Establishment For Its Failure to Recognize the Vaporization of Cannabis.

Of course, the people at the so-called compassion clubs have seen hundreds or even thousands of people who have used cannabis, whereas the so-called pharmacists who have taken a crash course from the people at Health Canada only know what they are told by people with no real world experience.

First, just what are the drug interactions with cannabis? Given the huge variety of pharmaceuticals taken by some seriously ill people, there is simply no way for anyone to keep track of all of the possible combinations of pharmaceuticals that might cause problems, but I am not aware of any serious interactions with cannabis. Moreover, among all of the drugs dispensed by pharmacies, cannabis is one of the few that has no lethal dose.

Second, many patients prefer smoking because it is so quick and easy, but how time flies when you are not in pain. Smoking may have some adverse effects, primarily for heavy smokers, but ingesting some medicines can also have adverse consequences.
See
 If Cannabis Didnt Cause Lung Cancer, They Would Tell Us Right? And If It Might Prevent It??? Or Cure It?? The Sound of Silence.
and
Counterblaste to DEA: Fallacious Pharmacology. "The contention that smoking cannot possibly be an acceptable route for the administration of a therapeutic substance is morality dressed up as science." by Peter Webster  

Although there are thousands of members of the so-called compassion societies HC has only managed to authorize 943 people to have medical cannabis. It still requires that a specialist be consulted if the patient does not have an approved disease or hasnt promised to die within a year.

Of those approved by HC, 695 have permits to grow their own, and HC has authorized 77 growers to produce it for other patients. Another 237 patients can get HCs weed directly from Prairie Plant Systems Inc., which grows it in an abandoned mine in Flin Flon, Manitoba. Their contract ends in December, but is expected to be extended by a year as Health Canada tries to find additional sources.
See
 Health Canada Gives $5.7 Million Contract to Company With No Experience to Grow Mediocre Weed for Medical Marijuana Research

Prairie Plant Systems new product contains about 14 per cent THC, whereas the strongest Dutch variety sold in pharmacies there has 18% THC. PPS cannabis was too weak and full of stems and leaves, and some patients even sent it back. In fairness to PPS, HC was so ignorant that it ordered the company to dilute its products. It has been allowed to increase the THC content, and it is now only buds.

An internal document from Health Canada says it could take up to three years to implement a national pharmacy distribution program. How time flies
See
 Canadian Medical Cannabis Patients Denounce Health Canadas War On Sick And Dying As New Survey Shows MARIJUANA LAWS A TOTAL FAILURE

My friend Philippe Lucas of the Vancouver Island Compassion Society www.Thevics.com in Victoria (or should that be the so-called Compassion Society) says, What we're talking about is a potential multimillion-dollar, multi-year program that would only reach 13 to 18 people in this entire province.
See
 Hypocrisy and Democracy: Raid on Medical Cannabis Research Facility Critical of Health Canadas Schwag Challenges Canadas Values. What Will The Politicians Say?

Presently PPS sends thirty-gram bags of dried buds via courier directly to patients or their doctors at a cost of C$150 each. (That would be about half the price of good weed from a Vancouver retailer  not a street-dealer in the same quantity).

It is not clear whether it will cost more from pharmacies, but this could be a real problem for GW Pharmaceuticals whose whole cannabis derivative, Sativex, was approved for sale in Canadian drug stores earlier this year.
See
 Program Notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report April 19, 2005 Sativex, Approved for Use In Canada. Proves Medical Value of Plant. Hires Prohibitionist Quack. Dangerous Pain Killers. Czar's Idiocy.

Sativex sells for C$150 per package containing the equivalent of only 30 doses and some patients require a lot of it to get relief. I have long argued that GWs business plan is predicated on a continuation of prohibition.

It is quite clear that this new HC pilot project is not going to have any real impact on the need for medical cannabis in the foreseeable future. Consequently, it really is medically and scientifically absurd. On the other hand, it is politically important because it is further proof that HC is still not in compliance with court orders to provide realistic access to medical cannabis. That is a threat to all of cannabis prohibition in Canada.
See
 Philippe Lucas Analysis of the Consequences of Health Canadas Failure to Obey the Ontario Courts Ruling On Medical Cannabis. Is Cannabis Legal in Canada?

It is also more proof that Dr. Lester Grinspoon is right when he argues that the full medical potential of cannabis can be realized only with its full legalization.
See
 Dr. Lester Grinspoon Warns About The Pharmaceuticalization of Cannabis, As GW Pharmaceutical Hits All Time High After Deal With Bayer. But Does It Need Prohibition In Order to Succeed?
